claim: On a real LLM's per-step output, single-best-path decoding (Viterbi/max-product) does not independently beat per-position marginal decoding (sum-product) on accuracy; the per-step output is too sharp (top-1 approx 0.92), so the two decoders converge.
carrier: chain-structured CRF/HMM multi-solution task (multi-variable, adjacent hard-exclusion constraints, deliberately multimodal posterior)
metric: whole-answer exact-match accuracy gap (MAP minus MPM); posterior modality (pmap, mass on MAP path); marginal infeasibility rate

real_llm.note: two decoders converge; LLM per-step output is near-unimodal

exact_emission_control_same_instances.note: with exact unary on the same instances the posterior is multimodal and the two decoders separate

random_synthetic_constructions.note: path's only clean advantage on random instances is staying globally feasible, not accuracy

adversarial_construction.mechanism: many individually-weak feasible solutions route through the same value at one position; their summed marginal outvotes the single best path, so per-position marginal flips while Viterbi keeps the best path
adversarial_construction.note: worst-case constructed potentials only; real LLM output does not fall into this distribution

conditions: Path decoding's independent accuracy advantage appears only when the posterior is genuinely multimodal and competing mass is shaped into a fan converging to one value at one position. Real LLM per-step output is too sharp to land there. Synthetic chain task with real-LLM read-out as unary; tested tasks have design caveats (local lexical cues, brittle whole-answer exact-match), direction holds but a cleaner multimodal natural-language task is still needed.
